headline.purpose: Geist display role; dashboard retains a more-specific desktop size and mobile override.

label.purpose: 14px, weight 600 for controls, navigation and field labels.

point-total.purpose: Actual earned total in the category ledger; 32px desktop and 26px mobile.

shadows.name: point-reset-dialog
shadows.purpose: Typed confirmation for resetting all society points.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disable animation and transition when reduced motion is requested.

motion.name: auth-maroon-ribbons
motion.value: none; static SEC reference ribbon SVG image
motion.purpose: Local reference-derived auth-story artwork remains still for all motion preferences; no animation loop or timed rendering.

motion.name: society-greeting
motion.purpose: The society greeting’s words are individual inline blocks that fade from opacity (0) to (1) and slide from horizontal offset (-16px) to (0) over (520ms), with `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` easing. Words stagger by (60ms), capped at (600ms). It plays once per authenticated session and resets on an authentication-required (401) response. Reduced-motion preference disables the greeting animation. The login ribbon remains static; earned-share bars and the completed PRT ring use the scoped draw motion described below.

motion.name: earned-share-bar
motion.purpose: Nonzero bars scaleX(0) to scaleX(1), origin left center; replay only on mount or society/point-period/category-value/earned-total key changes; reduced motion shows final state.

motion.name: prt-requirement-draw
motion.purpose: Met ring draws clockwise from top with stroke-dashoffset 100 to 0; key is society/point-period/met state; no replay from a higher already-met PRT amount; reduced motion shows final state.

motion.name: workspace-refresh
motion.purpose: Refresh icon while loading; disabled by reduced motion.

brand.preservation: Copied unchanged; retain proportions, contain fit, circular rounding, and no shrinking.

signIn.placement: Single logo in the story’s top brand; no duplicate logo above the form heading.

authStoryBackground.description: The user-pinned sign-in foundation is white (#ffffff), with equal desktop design/form columns. The static maroon artwork retains the SEC reference geometry, served locally as `public/society-ribbon.svg` from `https://ragnarok-flame-iota.vercel.app/brand/sign-in-ribbon.svg`. Its centered framing uses viewBox `570 -80 890 1070` and `xMidYMid meet`, with no artwork transform. The image is contained at opacity (0.88), inset (112px 2% 120px) within the left panel. The SVG’s own soft-ends mask uses edge-fade stops at (0.025) and (0.975), retaining more of the broad ribbon; there is no extra CSS mask, readability veil, or right-edge fade. The decorative image is pointer-inert, hidden from assistive technology, and has no animation, client rendering loop, or runtime external request. The panel contains only its top brand, artwork, and bottom description, “The home for Texas A&M engineering societies and SEC.” Mobile hides the artwork and description, retaining a compact brand header and bottom divider. The authenticated workspace keeps the same white foundation, pale rules, and muted maroon focus outline.

applicationReceipts.description: Application forms add a labeled confirmation-email field using the existing control style, with help text explaining the receipt destination and acceptance of an officer’s personal email or a society email. Receipt status is a normal paragraph (13px), with (16px 0 22px) margins and wrapping for long addresses; written messages distinguish queued, sent, and failed delivery while confirming that a failed email leaves the application saved. SEC review offers the existing secondary-button style to retry eligible unsent receipts, disabled while busy. These additions retain the ordinary form and record hierarchy.
applicationReceipts.fieldHelp: We’ll send a receipt here when you submit. An officer’s personal email or a society email works.
applicationReceipts.retryVisibility: Receipt exists, status is not SENT, and confirmation attempts are below 5.

dashboard.layoutDescription: The public navigation destination is Dashboard. SEC’s dashboard prioritizes the oldest five applications awaiting review with direct review actions and a full-queue link, then the earliest five upcoming or ongoing events with event-management actions and explicit check-in or manual High Impact award status. It also shows up to five enabled societies without an active PRT credit in the current point period and up to five enabled accounts awaiting setup across all point periods, with direct setup-link actions. Counts beside section headings reflect the full matching lists, and truncation text points to the complete destination. The full society points table remains available in the initially collapsed native disclosure, “All society point totals.” The society dashboard greets its account with “Hello, {display_name}” without an overview subtitle. It retains applications and recent attendance, shows the next three upcoming or ongoing events with a View events link, and replaces the former three-column trackers with the Society points ledger and separate PRT requirement.
dashboard.rowDescription: Dashboard action rows reuse ruled records and existing primary, secondary, or text actions. Row content allows shrinking with `min-width: 0`, while its direct action does not shrink. At (760px) and below, action rows stack their content and action vertically, align to the start, and use an (8px) gap. The native points-register disclosure summary is maroon, (13px), weight (650), with (12px 0 20px) padding. Repeated direct actions have descriptive accessible names; changing navigation destinations scrolls to the top.

events.scope: Current point period, not yet ended
events.status: Check-in availability or manual SEC award for High Impact.

prtFollowUp.scope: Enabled societies without an active, nonrevoked PRT credit of at least one point in the current point period

awaitingSetup.scope: Enabled, unactivated society accounts across all point periods

admin.counts: Full matching lists, independent of preview limits.

composition.description: Dashboard composition uses open sections separated by hairlines, with (26px 0) section padding and (24px 0) on mobile. The page headline is `clamp(34px, 3.5vw, 52px)` with (1.12) line height and (-0.04em) tracking, with mobile title sizing defined by the Typography section. Section headings are (22px), weight (680), reducing to (20px) on mobile; counts sit outside the heading in muted body type (14px, weight 500). Empty sections become one compact status line with a check icon and an optional destination action, using (18px 0) padding, without an extra heading or description. Each section keeps its accessible name and `data-count`. SEC has one primary header action: review the oldest pending application, otherwise manage the earliest upcoming event, otherwise create an event. The collapsed points-register content is also flat. The society greeting has the scoped entrance motion described below; the static login reference artwork remains unchanged.
composition.motion: Greeting words animate once per authenticated session; nonzero earned-share bars and the completed PRT ring draw on mount or keyed state changes; login ribbon remains static.
primaryHeaderActionPriority: Review next application: oldest pending submission
Manage next event: earliest upcoming event

loginHelp.description: The login combines account setup and password-reset help in one pale rose card (#fcf5f5) with a (1px #ead4d8) border, the input-matching (6px) radius, (18px) padding, and a (32px minmax(0, 1fr)) grid with a (12px) gap. A maroon KeyRound icon (17px) sits in a white circular holder (32px). The bold title is (14px) and body is (13px / 1.65); body margins are (7px 0 10px). The “Contact an SEC chair” action is maroon (12px, weight 650), with an ArrowRight icon, (8px) gap, and (36px) minimum height; hover underlines the label. Its mail link targets `society@sec.tamu.edu` with subject “SocietyHub account help.” Autofilled sign-in inputs retain white fill with a (1000px) inset white shadow, ink text and text fill, and a maroon caret through `:is(:autofill, :-webkit-autofill)`.

eventCalendar.description: Events offer List and Calendar views through native `aria-pressed` buttons in a white, line-bordered (6px) segmented control with a rose active fill. The view toolbar sits outside the content panel. The current point-period month calendar uses Central-time event windows, seven equal columns, and minimum day heights of (110px) desktop and (64px) mobile. Events render as continuous weekly spans in reusable nonoverlapping lanes, labeled once per weekly segment, with continuation arrows at clipped edges. Category fills use maroon, Standard rose, and High Impact slate, with a named legend and readable selected-day details. Date buttons retain roving keyboard focus, arrows and Home/End, a pale rose selected-day state, and a maroon circle for today; month navigation remains within scoped bounds.
eventCalendar.focus: Roving date buttons; arrow keys and Home/End.
eventCalendar.eventRendering: Continuous weekly spans; one label per segment; clipped edges have continuation arrows.

selectedDayDetails.description: Calendar selected-day details begin with a date block, date heading, and event count. Each event has a clear title (17px, weight 650; 15px mobile) beside its point amount, a category label underneath, clock/location facts, description text bounded to (70ch) at (13px / 1.65), and a distinct written check-in status with a dot. The day heading is (20px), reducing to (17px) on mobile. Event rows use (24px) vertical padding and a (24px) gap; mobile stacks details and actions with a (16px) gap and puts facts on separate lines.

administrativeForms.description: Administrative activity is an admin-only native disclosure, initially collapsed within an operational panel. Its summary uses Geist Variable (18px, weight 650), (17px) on mobile, an activity count, and a maroon chevron that rotates on open; expanded content is separated by (20px). Application authoring explicitly offers Save draft / Publish application, or Save published changes / Unpublish and save draft for published forms. The publication actions follow a top rule, (28px) top margin, and (20px) top padding. Drafts carry an amber label and a written not-published hint; the application list offers a primary Publish application action. Publication changes preserve the existing versioned form and saved submission behavior.

checkInQr.description: Event check-in QR artwork opens in a centered native dialog with a maximum width of (900px), white surface, panel radius, shadow (`0 24px 80px #1d001a30`), and dark backdrop (#21181b66). Its width is `min(900px, calc(100% - 48px))`, with a maximum height of `calc(100dvh - 48px)`; mobile uses (24px) total viewport clearance. The dialog traps Tab focus, restores the opener and page scrolling on close, and closes by its close control, Escape, or backdrop click. It retains a locally generated (1024px) maroon-on-white PNG download, sanitized event-derived filename, and current-link-bound image. Link replacement reports success locally with role status and explicitly invalidates earlier links/QRs; failure uses role alert and asks the user to reload before sharing. The event row arranges Edit and QR & link in a (72px 104px) action grid with an (8px) gap and a compact check-in toggle below; mobile uses (72px 104px 1fr) so the toggle shares the action row. Actions retain (44px) minimum height and `aria-pressed` toggle state.
checkInQr.linkBinding: Current check-in link only; invalidate outdated image.
checkInQr.focus: Trap Tab and restore opener on close.

loginLayout.description: Login uses equal white columns separated by a thin vertical rule. The left design panel has (48px 56px) padding, its SEC/SocietyHub brand at the top, centered contained artwork, and a short centered description at the bottom (14px, maximum 34ch). The form column uses (64px clamp(40px, 7vw, 112px)) padding and a (400px) form maximum width. At (760px) and below, art and description are hidden, leaving a compact brand header with (25px 24px) padding and a bottom divider; the form uses (36px 24px) padding and a (440px) maximum width.
loginLayout.descriptionText: The home for Texas A&M engineering societies and SEC.

applicationChoices.description: Choice-based application questions use separate required Choice N input rows rather than a multiline options editor. Rows use a (10px) gap with a flexible field and an icon remove control (44px minimum width, 44px minimum height). The choice group is capped at (640px) with (12px) row gaps and (20px 0 26px) margins. Add choice focuses the new field; removal focuses the preceding available choice. Each choice accepts up to (200) characters, with at least one and at most (30) choices; removal is disabled at one. Select and checkbox questions save their options array, while other question types normalize options to an empty array.

applicationReadOnly.description: Application content is aligned to a maximum width of (800px). On mobile, the containing panel header and back action stack with a (14px) gap. A submitted society application displays its saved question version and answers in a read-only definition list, with maroon checkmarks for selected multiple-choice values. Question labels are muted (12px, weight 600), answers are (14px) with (1.65) line height, and responses are separated by rules with (20px) vertical padding. A pale rose submission receipt (#fcf5f5), bordered (#ead4d8) and rounded (6px), uses (18px 20px) padding and a (30px) bottom margin; it shows submitted time, confirmation delivery status, and written metadata. Status remains visible above the responses. Drafts and changes-requested submissions retain editable fields when open; other existing read-only conditions still apply.

attendanceLedger.description: Attendance history is a ruled ledger with a compact date block, readable event details, and a prominent point amount rather than a tiny badge. A muted (13px) caption reports the active-record count. Rows use (24px) vertical padding and a (20px) gap; the date block is (56px) wide, and the point amount is Geist Variable (30px, weight 700, line height 1.15). Mobile uses (12px) gaps, a (44px) date block, (13px) event titles, and (26px) amounts, keeping the core row together unless correction controls need wrapping. Removed records retain their written state with muted date styling. The former “One society. One record” funding note is absent from the dashboard.
attendanceLedger.caption: Active-record count; 13px muted text.

societyPoints.description: Society points is a category ledger with Category, Earned, and Minimum columns, an actual earned-total heading, and an Attendance history action. Each ruled category row has a status icon, its point rate, and a (7px) bar showing that category’s share of total earned points, with no implied target. PRT uses maroon, Standard uses chart-standard rose, and High Impact uses chart-high-impact slate. Only PRT has a minimum of one point; Standard and High Impact display None. A separate (180px) ring shows the PRT requirement capped at 0 / 1 or 1 / 1, with (10px) strokes and an explicit requirement status; the ledger and accessible ring label retain the true PRT total even above one. Completed status uses semantic green. A zero total leaves all share bars empty and states that no points are recorded. Totals use only the selected society/current point period’s nonrevoked credits. The display has no timeline, forecast, category-filter controls, or monthly-data disclosure. Its nonzero share bars and completed requirement ring use a brief draw entrance while text and numbers stay constant.
societyPoints.shareMeaning: Category earned points / actual total earned points; zero total yields zero-width bars.

ring.label: Includes capped requirement and actual PRT total.

societyPoints.motion: Earned-share bars scale horizontally from (0) to (1), anchored at the left center, over (460ms) with `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` easing. The completed PRT ring draws clockwise from the top by changing stroke dash offset from (100) to (0) over (850ms) with `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` easing. These draw once on mount or when their keyed state changes: bars key society, point period, category value, and total; the ring keys society, point period, and whether the minimum is met. Increasing an already-met PRT total does not replay the ring. Zero bars and an unmet ring have no draw animation. Reduced-motion preference shows the final state immediately, with all numeric values and status text stable throughout.

pointReset.description: Point periods are controlled manually by SEC. Settings & audit provides Reset all society points, opening a native confirmation dialog that requires the exact text RESET POINTS. The white dialog has a (10px) radius, a line border, width `min(540px, calc(100% - 32px))`, (32px) padding (24px mobile), shadow (`0 24px 80px #211d2030`), and a blurred dark backdrop. It reports archived record/point counts before confirmation; busy controls prevent duplicate submission. Reset begins a new current points period for every society while preserving attendance history, events, forms, submissions, and QR links. Previous attendance records is a native disclosure with a (17px, weight 650) summary and an Export all history CSV action. Closing and reopening event check-in preserves the QR; an expired window opens the event editor so chairs can set a new window.

workspaceAccessibility.description: Form labels expose required state and associate hints with their controls. Check-in completion moves focus to its result heading. Notices and errors wrap long text and have accessible dismissal controls. The society directory offers search, readable labeled contact details with email/phone actions, and a ruled mobile list instead of the desktop table; contact detail columns stack on mobile. Primary buttons, icon actions, checkboxes, and event actions retain (44px) interaction targets.
workspaceAccessibility.navigation: Mobile dialog; trapped Tab, inert main, backdrop, Escape, focus restore, scroll lock.

receiptEmail.description: Application receipt email uses table-based structure and inline styling: a white content surface, pale rose surroundings and footer, maroon identity/action, dark ink, and muted descriptive copy. The SEC image is loaded through the configured HTTPS public site URL, rather than an invented mark. It records application and submission time without semester details, and explains that receipt is not approval or a point award. Arial/Helvetica/sans-serif is the intentional email-client fallback; Geist rendering in Gmail is not assumed.
receiptEmail.logo: Actual SEC mark using configured HTTPS site URL

societyRoster.description: The account-provisioning roster condenses repeated society names into one ruled row per group, with a canonical name, contact-response count, and one checkbox selecting every original response ID in that group. Grouping uses explicit aliases plus Unicode, case, ampersand, and punctuation normalization; related chapters and parent organizations stay distinct. Search includes the canonical name, original submitted names, and contacts. The native Contacts disclosure preserves each original name, submission date, and contact details, with (16px) vertical response padding and hairlines between responses; original-response metadata is muted (13px), with a (10px) bottom margin. The account-creation summary repeats the condensed canonical name and response count. This presentation groups records without merging or changing database data.
societyRoster.grouping: Explicit aliases plus NFKC/case/ampersand/punctuation normalization; no fuzzy matching.
societyRoster.row: Canonical name, original-response count, one checkbox for all response IDs.
societyRoster.relatedOrganizations: Chapters, teams and parent organizations remain separate unless an explicit alias matches.

components.name: Primary button
components.description: Main action with maroon hover and explicit disabled treatment.
components.css: .ds-button { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:11px 17px; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:6px; background:var(--maroon,#500000); color:#ffffff; font:600 14px/1.4 var(--sans,"Geist Variable","Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif); min-height:44px; cursor:pointer; transition:background .15s ease,box-shadow .15s ease; } .ds-button:hover:not(:disabled) { background:#712727; box-shadow:0 3px 8px #50000016; } .ds-button:disabled { opacity:1; cursor:not-allowed; background:#f1eded; border-color:var(--line,#e5e2df); color:var(--muted,#625b60); box-shadow:none; } .ds-button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--ds-focus,#8c4658); outline-offset:4px; } @media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-button { transition:none; } }

components.name: Secondary button
components.description: Supporting action with a ruled paper surface.
components.css: .ds-button { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; padding:11px 17px; border:1px solid transparent; border-radius:6px; background:var(--maroon,#500000); color:#ffffff; font:600 14px/1.4 var(--sans,"Geist Variable","Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif); min-height:44px; cursor:pointer; transition:background .15s ease,box-shadow .15s ease; } .ds-button:hover:not(:disabled) { background:#712727; box-shadow:0 3px 8px #50000016; } .ds-button:disabled { opacity:1; cursor:not-allowed; background:#f1eded; border-color:var(--line,#e5e2df); color:var(--muted,#625b60); box-shadow:none; } .ds-button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--ds-focus,#8c4658); outline-offset:4px; } .ds-secondary { background:var(--paper,#fff); color:var(--ink,#211d20); border-color:var(--line,#e5e2df); } .ds-secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { background:var(--tint,#f7f2f3); box-shadow:none; } @media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) { .ds-button { transition:none; } }

components.name: Labeled field
components.description: Persistent label with a white bordered control and mobile-readable type.
components.css: .ds-field { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:7px; color:var(--ink,#211d20); font:600 14px/1.6 var(--sans,"Geist Variable","Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif); } .ds-input { padding:11px 12px; min-height:43px; border:1px solid #9c9094; border-radius:6px; background:#fff; color:var(--ink,#211d20); font:400 16px/1.55 var(--sans,"Geist Variable","Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif); caret-color:var(--maroon,#500000); } .ds-input::placeholder { color:var(--muted,#625b60); } .ds-input:disabled { background:#f6f4f5; color:var(--muted,#625b60); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--ds-focus,#8c4658); outline-offset:4px; } @media(max-width:760px) { .ds-input { font-size:16px; } }

components.description: White workspace navigation with muted resting text and a transparent maroon active state marked by a thin left rule.
components.css: .ds-nav { padding:18px; background:var(--paper,#fff); border-right:1px solid var(--line,#e5e2df); display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:5px; } .ds-nav-item { padding:12px 14px; min-height:46px; border:0; border-radius:8px; background:transparent; color:#625b60; font:600 14px/1.6 var(--sans,"Geist Variable","Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif); text-align:left; cursor:pointer; transition:background .15s ease; } .ds-nav-item:not(.ds-active):hover { background:var(--tint,#f7f2f3); color:var(--maroon,#500000); } .ds-active { position:relative; background:transparent; color:var(--maroon,#500000); font-weight:650; border-radius:6px; } .ds-active::before { content:""; position:absolute; left:0; top:12px; bottom:12px; width:2px; background:var(--maroon,#500000); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--ds-focus,#8c4658); outline-offset:4px; } @media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce) {  .ds-nav-item { transition:none; } }

narrative.overview: White surfaces, maroon identity and actions, calm headings, and ruled records give societies and SEC a shared operating workspace. Readable records, explicit status, and efficient forms set the visual density. The public name is SocietyHub. Use the existing SEC circular logo copied unchanged from Delphi/public/sec_favicon.png; Nexus is an internal name only.
keyCharacteristics: Unified white surfaces with maroon identity and pale rose states.
Compact, readable records with clear hierarchy and tabular totals.
Restrained motion and explicit interaction states.

rules.name: The Status Rule
rules.body: Color reinforces a written status; it never replaces the status label.

dos: Do use white surfaces, pale rose interaction states, and thin rules for operational records.
Do retain labels, category names, and tabular totals when showing status or points.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep closed mobile navigation out of keyboard navigation.
donts: Don't replace written states with color alone.
Don't apply resting shadows to the flat record panels.
Don't substitute an invented mark for the supplied SEC logo.
